title_original: Was ‘Leaving Neverland’ TV award a factor in Bafta no-show for ‘Michael’?
excerpt_original: Objections by Jackson’s estate to the TV Bafta won by ‘Leaving Neverland’ may have played a part.

blocks.text: The decision by Universal Pictures not to enter Antoine Fuqua’s musical drama Michael into this year’s Bafta Film Awards could have had as much to do with objections by Jackson’s estate to the Bafta TV award won by Leaving Neverland in 2020 as the fallout from last year’s I Swear ceremony controversy.

The distributor is not required to give a reason for the decision and has not officially commented beyond a source citing “a number of factors” were at play in the decision taken by the filmmakers. Universal declined Screen ’s request to comment further.

Michael is about the early life of pop superstar Michael Jackson from the Jackson 5 to the early 1980s. The film has grossed over $1bn worldwide since being released by Lionsgate in North America and Universal internationally.
The film stars Jackson’s nephew Jaafar Jackson, Colman Domingo and Nia Long. John Logan wrote the script.

Leaving Neverland is a two-part documentary directed by Dan Reed and co-produced by Channel 4 and HBO in 2019. It explores the accusations of child abuse against Jackson by two men, Wade Robson and James Safechuck, when they were children in the 1990s. It won the Bafta TV award for best factual series in 2020.
Jackson repeatedly denied the accusations up until he died in 2009. His estate continues to strongly deny them.
Jackson’s estate is one of the major backers of Michael .

The decision not to enter Michael in the Bafta Film Awards has sparked a great deal of online speculation, with many suggesting that a contributing factor was also the events at last year’s ceremony. These saw John Davidson, who has Tourette’s Syndrome and whose life story inspired Kirk Jones’ I Swear , unwittingly utter a racial slur when Michael B Jordan and Delroy Lindo were presenting an award.
The BBC went on to initially broadcast the incident despite a two-hour delay.

At the time, Graham King of GK Films, who produced Michael with John Branca and John McClain, wrote a strongly worded response on social media. “For years, BAFTA and the BBC have repeatedly displayed cultural insensitivity and tone deafness,” he said in a statement posted to the GK Films’ Instagram account. “Their inability to take accountability for their actions or inactions is reckless and unacceptable.”

King has enjoyed significant Bafta success over the years on titles including The Aviator , winner of best film in 2005, and Bohemian Rhapsody , for which Rami Malek won Bafta’s leading actor award in 2019.
Online commentators and Jackson fans are also pointing to the Bafta TV award as a possible reason for the filmmakers to boycott the film awards.
Bafta declined Screen’s request for comment.

Further notable films that were eligible for this year’s Bafta Film Awards but have not been entered include Sony Pictures’ Jumanji : Open World , Resident Evil and Klara And The Sun ; Paramount’s Street Fighter and Focker In-Law ; Warner Bros’ Practical Magic 2 , Supergirl: Woman Of Tomorrow , The End Of Oak Street and Clayface ; Studiocanal’s How To Make A Killing ; and Mubi’s 2025 Golden Lion winner Father Mother Sister Brother.
